facts.raw_span: 2-week history of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules on his face, scalp, trunk, and extremities
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk along with keloidal plaques on the face
difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing for HIV was negative
Punch biopsy from arm showed: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells
Negative periodic acid–Schiff staining
Extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (hematoxylin-eosin stain)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses, is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques with histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses, are also consistent with Sweet syndrome.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with eczema herpeticum, although the negative HIV test and lack of other specific findings make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules and histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, could be consistent with bullous pemphigoid.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with dermatitis herpetiformis, although the lack of specific findings such as granular IgA deposits makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with erythema multiforme, although the lack of specific findings such as target lesions makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with psoriasis, although the lack of specific findings such as silvery scales makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, although the lack of specific findings such as fever and leukocytosis makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with subcorneal pustular dermatosis, although the lack of specific findings such as subcorneal pustules makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques with ulceration and bleeding, along with the presence of pustules, could be consistent with generalized pustular psoriasis, although the lack of specific findings such as silvery scales makes this diagnosis less likely.

The negative HIV test and negative periodic acid-Schiff staining suggest an infectious cause other than HIV or fungal infection, which could explain the patient's symptoms and histopathological findings.
